## 固定收益市場主線

9月23日，美國公債附息券殖利率全面上揚。油價盤中反彈後，美國企業活動調查遠強於預期，聯準會理事巴爾表示可能仍須升息，午後5年期公債標售又顯示需求疲弱，殖利率一路攀升。彭博按日期記錄的殖利率資料顯示，10年期上升15.2個基點至5.115%，5年期上升16.7個基點至5.004%。財政部標售$700億5年期公債，得標殖利率5.033%，比標售前交易殖利率高3.1個基點；盤中5年期殖利率自2007年以來首次突破5%。週二短天期公債因能源價格下跌而得到的喘息就此逆轉，市場同時面對更強的需求訊號與迫在眉睫的供給考驗。

油價從前一交易日外交消息引發的跌勢中盤中回升，是賣壓的起點，但不足以概括收盤行情。紐約時間下午5時的布蘭特原油期貨報$97.86，當日仍跌1.40%。伊朗總統重申荷莫茲海峽通行的條件，顯示美伊先前會談後能源風險仍在。美國9月綜合PMI初值升至58.4，創2021年7月以來最高，新訂單加速，投入成本大幅上升。聯準會理事巴爾表示，通膨風險升高、勞動市場風險減退。這些變化讓標售疲弱有了比原油更廣泛的政策背景。

賣壓也傳至美國公債以外。週三市場報導顯示，德國與英國10年期公債殖利率均上升，美元走強；紐約時間下午5時，標普500指數跌0.76%。美國投資等級債利差小幅擴大，高收益債利差則明顯擴大，但大型發行人仍完成融資。軟銀以該公司紀錄最高的借款殖利率，完成約$110億跨美元與歐元的高收益債發行，讓AI建設的融資成本成為當天另一條獨立主線。

## 美國數據、聯準會訊號與公債供給推升殖利率

美國公債一開始因油價反彈而承壓，逆轉週二能源價格下跌帶來的通膨緩解。報導指出，布蘭特原油在美國交易時段重返$100以上。伊朗總統裴澤斯基安在聯合國表示，只要制裁與美國封鎖仍在，德黑蘭就不會允許船隻自由通過荷莫茲海峽。伊朗雖表示願意恢復談判，但海峽重開條件仍有爭議，削弱了前一天美伊進行3小時討論所帶來的期待。美國能源部長另稱，政府正與煉油業者討論自願限制柴油出口；白宮則否認計畫實施90天出口禁令的報導。這些仍屬政策討論，燃料出口並未因此發生已確認的變動。

隨後公布的標普全球9月美國PMI初值，提供更明確的國內成長訊號。綜合產出指數由8月的56.0升至58.4，高於預估的55.2，創逾5年新高。製造業由53.9跳升至57.0，優於市場預期的53.6；服務業由56.5升至58.7，也高於預期的56.0。兩個產業同步增強，並非單一產業撐起整體表現。數據雖仍是初值，但其廣度顯示，單靠能源因素不足以解釋殖利率上升。

新訂單指數由55.2升至58.2，為2022年3月以來最高，製造業與服務業皆有成長。未完成訂單創2022年5月以來最高，供應商交貨延遲則為2022年7月以來最普遍；就業以逾4年來最快速度增加。投入價格指數從59.9升至66.4，創2022年10月以來最高。受訪企業提到燃料與運輸成本，也有部分企業指出薪資上漲。標普全球認為PMI對應約5%的年化GDP成長；亞特蘭大聯準銀行GDPNow估計為5.1%，相較之下，第2季實際成長1.5%。價格與產能細項顯示需求正擠壓資源，不只是企業從先前低潮回升。

具投票權的聯準會理事巴爾提供了明確的政策判斷：通膨偏離2%目標的風險上升，勞動市場風險下降，可能仍須進一步調整政策，才能及時讓通膨回到目標。聯邦公開市場委員會上週一致升息25個基點，將目標區間調至3.75%至4.00%；18名決策者中有16人認為年底前可能至少還需升息一次。路透社解讀巴爾措辭暗示至少再升息兩次，但他未給出時間表。巴爾發言後，短期利率期貨反映10月27日至28日會議升息機率約70%，高於週三稍早約55%；較廣泛市場報導中的交換市場，則已充分反映未來一年升息3次、每次25個基點，並大量避險第4次升息的可能。兩者涉及不同期限與工具，不能當成同一場會議的機率估計。

白宮的看法相反。國家經濟會議主任哈塞特認為，近期年化核心通膨率為2%，不構成繼續升息的理由；他批評並非由川普總統任命卻主張升息的官員，特別點名前主席鮑爾與巴爾，並稱主席沃許正管理一個異常黨派化的聯準會。這是對央行決策的政治批評，並未改變委員會宣示的政策判斷方式。包含沃許、鮑爾與巴爾在內的全體決策者，上週都投票支持升息。週三另有報導指波士頓聯準銀行總裁柯林斯支持最近一次升息，聖路易聯準銀行總裁穆薩萊姆認為可能仍須升息；本次報導時段中提供具體新判斷條件的則是巴爾。

午後標售使已經展開的跌勢加劇。財政部發行$700億5年期公債，得標殖利率5.033%，標售前交易參考值為5.002%，尾差3.1個基點。依彭博自2018年起的紀錄，這是5年期公債第二差的標售結果，僅次於2022年6月。投標倍數2.21；間接投標人取得54.3%，直接投標人29.9%，交易商承接15.8%。得標殖利率為2006年以來該天期最高。這是已實現的需求結果，與財政部另外宣布的舊債買回不同。17週期國庫券以4.135%標售，投標倍數2.81；2年期浮動利率債投標倍數為2.63，但這兩項短期融資結果沒有改變附息公債殖利率曲線的主線。

彭博同一日期的殖利率資料顯示，2年期上升14.2個基點至4.898%，5年期上升16.7個基點至5.004%，10年期上升15.2個基點至5.115%，30年期上升10.0個基點至5.401%。短天期與中期調整較大，2年與30年期殖利率差縮小4.2個基點至50.3個基點。10年期實質殖利率上升13.2個基點至2.77%，損益兩平通膨率上升2.0個基點至2.345%；在同來源的拆解中，名目10年期殖利率當日漲幅大部分來自實質殖利率，能源衝擊仍是重要政策風險。彭博盤中曾描述10年期殖利率在上升近17個基點後接近5.13%，30年期約5.4%；這些盤中數字並非上述日期資料的精確收盤值。

住房融資成本在週三美債收盤前已經升高。美國房貸銀行協會指出，截至9月18日當週，30年期固定房貸合約利率升15個基點至7.12%，為2024年5月以來最高。申請件數繼前週下跌4.1%後再跌1.5%；整體申請指數由230.8降至227.3，再融資指數由627.1降至611.0，購屋申請指數由156.2降至154.9。不過，5年期浮動房貸利率反向下降13個基點至6.1%，當週融資成本變化並不一致。Redfin的Daryl Fairweather認為7%是心理阻力，Nationwide則預期利率將在年底前維持於該水準附近。這筆較早公布的數據顯示，最新一輪公債殖利率上升前，住房市場已受到高利率限制。

財政部宣布，將於週四依財長貝森特擴大的買回計畫，買入最多$60億、剩餘期限20至30年的公債。規模是8月最初公布$20億的3倍；財政部其後曾表示，此類操作至少會加倍。公告後長天期公債仍下跌，當時30年期殖利率一度升至報導中的盤中高點5.38%。先前一次擴大後的操作上限為$60億，投資人提出$105億賣盤，實際買回約$52億；官員稱未用足額度是因具競爭力的報價不足。國際金融協會週三指出，次級市場買回可提供暫時緩解，卻無法解決債務上升的財政成因。週四的$60億是操作上限，實際買入金額仍待結果確認。

美元走強也是美國利率重新定價的表現。當日市場報導中，彭博美元即期指數漲0.6%，達7月底以來最高；紐約時間下午5時的美元指數則升0.68%至101.115。黃金期貨跌1.16%至$4,325.80，標普500指數跌0.76%至7,706.03。同一時點的市場資料顯示，那斯達克100指數跌幅不到0.01%，半導體股則漲0.81%；較高折現率壓抑整體風險資產，但股市反應並不一致。iShares 20年以上美國公債ETF下跌1.6%，收在紀錄低點$80.46。其股價較2020年高峰已跌逾一半，但今年以來含配息的總報酬為負4.8%，小於股價本身7.7%的跌幅。

## 能源衝擊下的全球景氣與政策分歧

經濟合作暨發展組織（OECD）最新期中展望，將通膨問題擴展到美國以外。該組織將2026年全球成長預測由2.8%上修至2.9%，仍低於2025年的3.4%；2027年則由3.1%下修至3.0%。G20通膨預測方面，2026年由4.0%上修至4.1%，2027年由3.1%大幅上修至3.6%；除中國與沙烏地阿拉伯外，所有G20經濟體的2027年通膨預測均上調。AI投資支撐近期活動，但能源成本持續偏高削弱較後期前景。

OECD預測聯準會今年再升息一次，歐元區、澳洲與南韓小幅續升，日本也將進一步升息；英國央行與加拿大央行則暫時維持利率。它預估美國2026年、2027年分別成長2.2%與2.1%，通膨分別為3.6%與2.6%。其下行情境把能源壓力、強烈聖嬰現象、公債殖利率上升與AI投資報酬不如預期合併考量：若同時出現，2027年全球成長可能少0.7個百分點、通膨多1.1個百分點。這是情境推演，而非基準預測。OECD也警告各國政府，公債殖利率升高使整頓公共財政更迫切。

歐洲自己的9月企業調查，說明歐洲央行不能把能源衝擊直接當成停止升息的理由。歐元區綜合PMI由52.0升至53.1，市場原預估降至51.7；這是逾3年來最好表現。服務業意外改善，德國活動以2025年10月以來最快速度成長，法國則創逾2年最大增幅。標普全球的Chris Williamson指出，AI與國防支出支撐製造業；製造業與服務業的訂單也顯示動能可延續。成本與借款利率上升仍可能壓抑消費，但新數據使歐洲央行面對更穩固的當前活動基礎。歐元仍走弱，一度觸及$1.1409，選擇權部位也愈發偏向下檔；市場人士將壓力歸因於美國升息預期再起及歐洲的能源曝險。

歐洲央行首席經濟學家雷恩對升息理由提出限制。他說能源價格飆升尚未帶來顯著薪資壓力，減輕了整體通膨透過薪資固化的疑慮。但能源價格走勢至2027年年中仍接近央行不利情境，之後才朝基準情境靠攏；天然氣庫存約70%，比歷史平均低16個百分點。歐元區8月通膨高於3%，部分經濟學家預期年底可能達4%。雷恩認為，扣除風險溢價後，市價所隱含的明年利率高點僅略高於3%，約相當於再升息兩次；直接按市價推算升息3或4次，會高估市場對政策利率的預期。這項區分並未消除能源風險。

英國則同時面對成長放緩與財政空間收窄。OECD預估2026年與2027年經濟分別成長1.1%和1.0%，平均通膨率分別為3.1%和2.6%；認為英國央行可將3.75%政策利率維持至2027年年中，再降息25個基點，但敦促政府加強控制並調整支出。經濟學家估計，借款成本與通膨上升，已使財政大臣John Healey用以符合財政規則的£236億緩衝空間減半。首相Andy Burnham重申英國對債市依賴過深，維持先前稱英國受制於債市的批評，同時表示希望打造更有生產力的國家。10月28日預算案將須在利息成本惡化之際容納國防及社會支出計畫。報導中的30年期英國公債殖利率為5.76%，低於前週接近6%的高點；當日全球殖利率上升，本身不足以證明英國出現新的特有財政拋售。

南非已作出升息決定。南非準備銀行一致決議將基準利率提高25個基點至7.25%，為今年第二次升息，符合受訪22名經濟學家中19人的預期。總裁Lesetja Kganyago表示，當前衝擊消退時，通膨須回到3%目標。8月通膨由4.3%微升至4.4%；央行將2026年平均通膨預測由4.0%上修至4.4%，2027年由3.8%上修至4.0%。今年假設油價由每桶$82升至$90，明年由$75升至$80。官員也曾考慮按兵不動與升息50個基點。Kganyago稱投票前政策僅略具限制性，並警告持續衝擊較可能引發第二輪效應。報導中的約翰尼斯堡午後，南非幣貶約1.3%至每美元16.39，10年期公債殖利率升9個基點至8.90%。

面對相同外部壓力，印尼選擇不同做法。印尼央行連續第3次會議維持5.75%關鍵利率，符合36名經濟學家中33人的預期；總裁Destry Damayanti則提高留住資本的誘因。央行將一般避險交換交易溢價最多調降25%，境內無本金交割遠期交易溢價最多調降30%，資金持有愈久折減幅度愈大；同時維持境外與境內干預，包括在次級市場買入政府債券。決策後，印尼盾升值0.4%至每美元約17,800，債券維持先前漲勢。Destry認為現行利率足以維持穩定，但也指出交易時油價高於$100、全球通膨升高，聯準會可能繼續升息。印尼8月通膨3.2%，接近央行1.5%至3.5%區間上緣；銀行放款年增13.65%，高於央行8%至12%的預期。Lombard Odier的Homin Lee仍預期，若能源與聯準會不確定性持續，印尼12月將升息25個基點。

新加坡8月通膨提供另一項亞洲物價觀察。核心通膨年增2.2%，符合市場預期，為2024年9月以來最高；食品、零售與服務價格漲勢加快。整體通膨為2.3%，公用事業與其他燃料價格上漲6.1%。新加坡金融管理局與貿易部認為風險偏上行，因油價、天候及進口投入成本可能在未來幾季轉嫁。金管局預估今年核心通膨為1.5%至2.5%，約從2027年年中開始放緩；下次政策決定預定於10月中公布。目前數字反映輸入性通膨壓力，但尚不足以預先確定匯率政策會再調整。

日本因銀週假期休市，公債市場要到週四重開，才會反映美國債市跌勢。日圓連跌4天，在日本央行最近升息至1.25%後又引發干預疑慮。Eastspring Investments投資組合經理Rong Ren Goh另提出跨市場需求判斷：殖利率超過4%的30年期日本公債，若換匯至包括美元在內的已開發市場貨幣，匯率避險後殖利率可能高於同類基準貨幣債券100至200個基點。他指出，日本2年與30年期殖利率差超過200個基點，其他主要已開發市場平均約80個基點；他正透過高品質企業債與武士債增加超長天期日本曝險。這是Rong Ren Goh的投資策略與跨市場比較；日本公債週四重開後的實際表現仍有待觀察。

## AI融資面對更嚴峻的信用市場

軟銀這筆大型融資已從初步詢價走到最終定價。該日本集團為AI布局發行約$110億美元與歐元高收益債，按彭博統計成為全球企業高收益債最大借款人。其中，$10億、3.5年期美元債殖利率8.625%；$45億、5.5年期為9.25%；另有$45億、7.5年後到期債券為9.75%。歐元債共€10億，分為4年與6年期，較長天期殖利率8%。美元各券殖利率均為軟銀在該幣別融資最高，較長天期歐元債也創其同天期歐元借款紀錄。

亞洲午後詢價顯示，$100億美元債收到逾$300億訂單，使軟銀得以將殖利率調降至初步行銷區間以下。需求深厚，但在美國公債基準利率上升後，軟銀承擔的絕對融資成本仍遠高於以往。它對OpenAI的承諾接近$650億，先前已擴大有擔保與過橋融資；此次無擔保發債因此檢驗債券投資人願承接多少AI曝險。高盛策略師估計，2026年全球AI相關債務發行超過$5,750億。軟銀5年期信用違約交換成本本月升至2025年4月以來最高，與熱烈認購並存，反映投資人疑慮。

規模較小的Digital Drive交易，則呈現AI建設風險的另一種定價。這家由Blue Owl Capital關係企業、Cedarwood Investment Group與PowerHouse Data Centers贊助的開發商，發行$11億5年期高收益債，價格為每面額$1的98.5美分，殖利率9.25%，較同等評級債券平均高約2.7個百分點。資金支援維吉尼亞州里奇蒙附近76兆瓦資料中心園區，已由CoreWeave依15年、$29.4億合約全數承租，預計2027至2028年開始營運。標普給予BB-評級，認為依賴單一投機等級租戶是主要風險。長約支撐預期收入，但建設與租戶信用風險仍決定融資價格。

成熟AI借款人的避險活動，也在改變市場結構。標普道瓊指數的Nicholas Godec援引DTCC資料指出，近6個月輝達債務信用保護交易量達$69億，前6個月僅$6.4億。輝達6月發行$250億債券後，信用違約交換流動性增加，是其週一納入最新一系列CDX投資等級指數的主要原因；SpaceX也在類似規模的高評級債券發行後加入。隨著借款與基礎設施承諾增加，輝達信用保護成本今年翻倍，投資人和銀行利用合約對沖累積曝險。CDX換券本身連同美債殖利率上升，也促使指數利差擴大；成分變化不能全解讀為每家借款人信用同步惡化。

整體美國信用市場轉弱，但交易仍能完成。收盤時投資等級利差小幅擴大，高收益債利差明顯擴大；納入配息的報酬計算下，LQD跌1.14%、HYG跌0.74%，基金虧損也包含底層殖利率上升的影響。Peloton可能首次發債，反映個別借款條件仍在試探。高盛已向投資人探詢約$8億有擔保債券、殖利率約8%的意向，但尚未決定是否正式發行。Peloton於2024年曾使用$10億槓桿貸款，定價約高於基準利率6個百分點。這次債券殖利率仍是行銷討論，並非成交結果。

其他已完成或已宣布的發行提供較常規的定價參考。AerCap Funding完成$15億優先無擔保債，平均分為2030年到期、票息5.500%及2033年到期、票息5.875%兩批，由AerCap Holdings與指定子公司提供全額保證；資金可用於飛機資產融資或再融資、償還債務及一般公司用途。美國固定收益市場截止時間之後，加拿大皇家銀行另宣布$15億具不可存續觸發條款的次順位資本債。票息至2031年10月1日為4.67%，之後至2036年10月1日改為複利CORRA加1.16個百分點；自2031年起按面額贖回須獲監管核准並通知。預定10月1日交割及票息重設條件界定這筆銀行資本曝險，較晚發布的消息並非週三美債走勢的原因。

派拉蒙天空之舞收購華納兄弟探索的融資推進了一步。相關訴訟和解後，花旗安排週四向貸款投資人介紹這筆$1,100億收購案。已承銷待分銷的融資包括約$300億投資等級債、$75億投資等級貸款及約$120億第二順位債。交易結構與收購對利率的曝險先前已確立，新的投資人電話會議標誌直接行銷啟動，最終承銷價格仍待確定。另方面，通訊公司Bird.com取得由摩根大通牽頭的$4.5億融資，包括$4億定期貸款與$5,000萬循環額度。執行長Robert Vis表示，資金將用於向股東及現任、前任員工發放股利，讓他們取得流動性而不必在次級市場出售股票；他稱去年EBITDA為$1.65億，美國收入約占總額70%。這筆貸款用於分配現金，而非新增營運資產。

## 重整條件與主權融資動向

泰晤士水務的優先債權人正準備提高讓步幅度，試圖避免政府啟動特別管理程序。包括Elliott、Silver Point與Farallon的London & Valley Water，在與監管機構Ofwat及官員討論後，計畫最快10月提出修訂方案。討論中的債務減記比例由30%升至約35%，新增股本由£33.5億增至約£35億，另有約£65.5億債務配合。條件仍待談判；對負債逾£180億的公用事業而言，債權人分攤損失的變化才是本次新進展。

債權人另提議設立逾£10億專項績效基金，比先前提出用以替代部分監管罰款的金額至少多£2億。泰晤士水務預計到2030年代結束前，因漏水、汙水外洩及其他未達標事項，須支付最多£8億績效罰款；正常情況下，這些款項會用來調降客戶帳單。債權人主張，把更多資金專款投入改善營運，比以罰款方式取出現金，更能讓公司恢復投資等級。環境或飲水違規的法律罰金則另行計算，仍須支付。方案還將給予政府一股黃金股、加強監督，並在擬議的9年整頓期禁止業主發放股利。議員反對將控制權交給債權人，政府也在考慮特別管理。Teneo先前估計，在該情境下，A類債權人每£1債權可能僅收回約50便士，實際仍取決於營運表現；那是情境估計，不是已談妥的重整回收率。

瑞士議員則作出會影響銀行債權人的實際資本決定。上議院以29票對16票通過規定，要求瑞銀以高品質股權資本，支應海外子公司最高相當於其價值90%的金額，略低於政府原提議的100%。瑞銀估計境內單位需增加約$160億普通股權第一類資本（CET1），高盛與花旗分析師估計負擔約$170億。瑞銀原主張採較寬鬆方案，更多使用額外第一類資本（AT1）或有可轉換債。上議院表決使這條路收窄，現有瑞銀AT1債因新增供給前景減弱，一度上漲0.3美分至每面額$1的98.36美分。瑞銀表示將繼續反對法案。下議院仍須表態，最終規定可能要到2027年之後才出爐，也可能付諸公投。

美國總統直接參與委內瑞拉債務討論。國務卿魯比歐表示，川普總統與臨時總統Delcy Rodríguez在9月22日招待會討論重整，也談及未來選舉所需的制度步驟。魯比歐說美國希望協助穩定經濟，但債務處理必須妥當。委內瑞拉主權與國營石油公司PDVSA違約債券合計約$600億；分析師估計的更廣泛債務與請求權達$1,500億至$2,000億，包含應計利息及仲裁請求等其他負債。債券本金與總請求權的差別，攸關潛在債權人回收。兩國此前已開始與多邊機構接觸，泛美開發銀行擬議的$25億貸款仍遭部分董事反對。會面未產生重整條款或融資核准。

匈牙利公債呈現不同的外資需求。央行早已決定自2028年起將長期通膨目標由3%降至2.5%；新訊息是資金流入規模及其對殖利率的影響。德意志銀行估計，外資今年迄今買入$135億當地債券，其中$100億發生於4月選舉之後。債務管理機構AKK指出，8月底外資持有比例達34%，為2019年以來最高。匈牙利10年期殖利率約5.64%，低於波蘭的6.16%及羅馬尼亞的7.29%；投資人將新目標與可能的歐元趨同連結。不過，需求有賴財政執行：2026年赤字預估占GDP的7.5%，投資人仍等待2027年預算與中期計畫。約€160億歐盟資金可能解凍也是支撐因素，尚非已到位款項。

中國則提供較即時的貨幣市場措施。中國人民銀行宣布，9月28日至10月8日中秋與國慶假期前後，每日可提供最高人民幣1兆元、約$1,490億的隔夜逆回購，但未列明個別操作日或借款成本。銀行間債券市場預定9月25日至27日及10月1日至7日休市，這項機制為較長假期的現金與交割需求提供後盾。印尼央行同期運用避險優惠與買債因應外部利率壓力，屬另一種本地政策回應；中國此舉則處理假期流動性，並非政策利率調整。

美中貿易風險在債市截止時間後出現變化。財長貝森特表示，在習近平訪問華府前與中國副總理何立峰討論後，美中9月23日同意將釜山協議延長至1月10日。貝森特稱雙方也探討，能否以更全面協議取代一系列較窄的安排。延長期限降低現有架構近期失效的風險；消息公布太晚，無法解釋已結束的美國固定收益交易，更全面的協議仍是目標，尚未談成。

## 後續市場觀察

週四財政部買回操作將揭示，在20至30年期公債最高$60億額度下實際買入多少，以及投資人願以什麼價格賣出。接下來的7年期標售，則是繼5年期標售尾差3.1個基點後另一項附息公債需求考驗。兩項結果有助判斷週三的標售疲弱是否僅屬單次現象，以及市場是否持續要求新發公債提供更高殖利率。

9月24日美國初領與續領失業救濟金人數，將檢驗巴爾對勞動市場風險減退的判斷。現有預測為初領20.1萬人、前值19.6萬人；續領175萬人、前值173萬人。週五耐久財報告預估整體訂單下降0.4%，扣除運輸設備後增長0.6%，扣除飛機的非國防資本財訂單增長0.5%；在PMI訂單全面上升後，這種分化值得檢驗。9月密西根大學消費者信心終值預估顯示，1年期通膨預期4.6%、5年期3.4%，可直接觀察投入成本上漲是否進入家庭較長期的預期。聯準會的威廉斯與巴金兩位地區聯準銀行總裁預定週四發言；巴金先前以供給衝擊是否反覆發生提出條件，後續補充尤其值得注意。

美伊談判仍須解決制裁、美國封鎖及荷莫茲海峽自由通行的爭議。對通膨前景而言，船舶實際通行與出口持續恢復，比再一次宣布會談更有分量。川習峰會將在新延長的貿易架構下舉行；投資人可觀察兩國領袖是否在1月10日之前敲定更廣泛的關稅、投資或技術條款。這兩項前瞻發展均不屬於週三已完成的債市收盤行情。

其他市場方面，日本假期後重開，可觀察日本公債與日圓如何消化日本央行較高的政策利率水準，以及週三美國利率部位的拋售。挪威央行勢均力敵的決策與瑞典央行預期維持利率的決定，都將於週四公布，並附更新預測，可檢驗能源成本上升是否讓北歐利率路徑分化。泰晤士水務的修訂債權人方案、匈牙利2027年預算計畫，以及派拉蒙多部分融資的實際行銷條件，則是彼此獨立的信用與主權債觀察重點；後續數字、批准與時點將決定債權人曝險如何變化。

overall_summary.headline: 美國景氣強、聯準會偏鷹且標售需求疲弱，公債全面下跌
overall_summary.session_narrative:
9月23日，美國公債附息券全面下跌。10年期殖利率上升15.2個基點至5.115%，5年期上升16.7個基點至5.004%。9月美國綜合PMI初值升至58.4，新訂單加快、投入成本大幅上升。聯準會理事巴爾認為通膨風險升高、勞動市場風險減退，可能仍須進一步升息。其後$700億5年期公債以5.033%得標，比標售前交易殖利率高3.1個基點，為已展開的跌勢增添需求疲弱的明確證據。10年期名目殖利率當日漲幅主要來自實質殖利率上升。

伊朗重申荷莫茲海峽通行條件，油價盤中重返$100以上，但紐約時間下午5時布蘭特原油仍跌1.40%。美元走強，標普500指數跌0.76%；美國投資等級債利差小幅擴大，高收益債利差明顯擴大。軟銀仍為AI布局完成約$110億美元及歐元高收益債融資，美元借款殖利率卻創公司紀錄。接下來的7年期標售與週四財政部買回，將檢驗公債供給壓力是否持續。

section_summaries.summary: 美國企業調查強勁、巴爾主張升息及$700億5年期標售出現3.1個基點尾差，接連推高殖利率，5年期盤中突破5%。伊朗對荷莫茲海峽通行提出條件，使能源風險未退，儘管布蘭特原油在下午5時觀察點仍收低。美國信用利差擴大、軟銀借款成本創紀錄，顯示重新定價已超出公債。

section_summaries.section_title: 美國數據、聯準會訊號與公債供給推升殖利率
section_summaries.summary: 9月綜合PMI初值由56.0跳升至58.4，訂單、就業及投入價格同步走強。巴爾認為通膨風險上升，聯準會可能仍須升息；其發言後10月升息機率提高。$700億5年期標售得標殖利率高於標售前交易值3.1個基點，使美債跌勢加劇。10年期殖利率上升15.2個基點至5.115%，主要由實質殖利率帶動；每週房貸利率升至7.12%，顯示週三收盤前住房市場已有壓力。

section_summaries.section_title: 能源衝擊下的全球景氣與政策分歧

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries sold off across the coupon curve on September 23 as a much stronger U.S. business survey, a Federal Reserve governor's call for further tightening and a poorly received 5-year auction successively raised the cost of holding duration. The 10-year yield rose 15.2 basis points to 5.115% in Bloomberg's dated yield history, while the 5-year climbed 16.7 basis points to 5.004%. The $70 billion auction cleared at 5.033%, 3.1 basis points above its when-issued yield, and pushed the intermediate sector through 5% for the first time since 2007 in intraday trading. The day reversed Tuesday's short-end relief and left investors confronting both a stronger demand picture and an immediate test of Treasury supply.

Oil's intraday recovery from the previous session's diplomacy helped start the selling, but did not describe the whole close: the Brent future in the 5 p.m. New York market observation was $97.86, down 1.40% on the day. Iran's president then reiterated conditions on passage through the Strait of Hormuz, keeping the energy risk alive despite the earlier U.S.-Iran talks. September's flash U.S. composite PMI reached 58.4, its highest since July 2021, with faster new orders and a sharp increase in input costs. Governor Michael Barr said inflation risks had risen as labor-market risks receded. Those developments gave the auction weakness a policy backdrop wider than crude alone.

The rise in yields extended beyond Treasuries. German and British 10-year rates rose in Wednesday's market reporting, the dollar strengthened and the S&P 500 fell 0.76% at the 5 p.m. observation. U.S. investment-grade spreads widened modestly and high-yield spreads widened noticeably, even while large issuers still completed financings. SoftBank priced its roughly $11 billion cross-currency junk-bond sale at record borrowing yields for the company, making the cost of funding the AI buildout a second, separate story of the session.

## U.S. Data, Fed Signals and Supply Push Yields Higher

The Treasury decline began as an oil rebound renewed inflation concern after Tuesday's energy-led relief. Brent was reported back above $100 during U.S. trading, and Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian said at the United Nations that Tehran would not permit freedom of navigation through Hormuz while sanctions and a U.S. blockade remained. His statement qualified hopes raised by the three-hour U.S.-Iran discussion reported the previous day. Iran said it was ready to resume talks, but the conditions for reopening the waterway remained disputed. The U.S. energy secretary separately said the administration was working with refiners on voluntary limits to diesel exports; the White House denied a report of a planned 90-day export ban. Those were policy discussions, not a realized change in fuel shipments.

The September flash S&P Global survey then supplied a much less ambiguous domestic growth signal. The composite output index rose to 58.4 from 56.0 in August, above a 55.2 forecast and its highest reading in more than five years. Manufacturing jumped to 57.0 from 53.9, against a 53.6 consensus; services climbed to 58.7 from 56.5, against 56.0 expected. Both sectors therefore strengthened, rather than one carrying a weak counterpart. The data were preliminary readings, but their breadth made a simple energy-only account of the yield move inadequate.

New orders rose to 58.2 from 55.2, the strongest since March 2022, with gains across manufacturing and services. Backlogs reached their highest since May 2022, and supplier delivery delays were the most widespread since July 2022. Employment increased at its fastest pace in more than four years. Input prices rose to 66.4 from 59.9, the highest since October 2022; respondents cited fuel and transportation, with some also reporting higher wages. S&P Global said the PMI corresponded to roughly 5% annualized GDP growth. The Atlanta Fed's GDPNow estimate stood at 5.1%, compared with actual second-quarter growth of 1.5%. The survey's price and capacity details matter alongside its output level because they describe demand pressing against resources, not simply firms recovering from an earlier lull.

Barr, a voting Fed governor, gave the market a named policy response. He said risks to the inflation target had increased while risks to the labor market had receded, and that further adjustments were likely needed to return inflation to 2% in a timely way. The committee unanimously raised its target range 25 basis points to 3.75%-4.00% the previous week; 16 of 18 policymakers had indicated at least one more increase would probably be needed before year-end. Reuters interpreted Barr's wording as suggesting at least two more increases, although he supplied no timing. Short-rate futures put the probability of a hike at the October 27-28 meeting at about 70% after his remarks, from roughly 55% earlier Wednesday. Swaps in broader market reporting fully reflected three quarter-point moves over the next year, with substantial hedging against a fourth. Those are different horizons and instruments, rather than interchangeable estimates of a single meeting.

The White House offered an opposing assessment. National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett said a recent annualized core inflation rate of 2% did not justify more increases and criticized officials who had not been appointed by President Donald Trump for advocating them. He singled out former chair Jerome Powell and Barr while arguing that Chair Kevin Warsh was managing an unusually partisan Fed. Hassett's view was political criticism of the central bank's decision, not a change in its stated reaction function. The whole rate-setting committee, including Warsh, Powell and Barr, had voted for last week's increase. Boston Fed President Susan Collins and St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem were also reported Wednesday as supporting the latest move or seeing possible further increases, respectively; the detailed new conditions in this window came from Barr.

The afternoon auction amplified a selloff already under way. The Treasury sold $70 billion of 5-year notes at 5.033%, against a 5.002% when-issued reference. The 3.1-basis-point tail was the second-worst 5-year result in Bloomberg's records since 2018, exceeded only by June 2022. The bid-to-cover ratio was 2.21; indirect bidders took 54.3%, direct bidders 29.9% and dealers 15.8%. The clearing yield was the highest for the tenor since 2006. It was a realized demand result, distinct from the Treasury's separately announced buyback of older debt. A 17-week bill auction cleared at 4.135% with 2.81 cover, and the 2-year floating-rate note attracted 2.63 cover, but neither short-funding result altered the coupon-curve story.

In the dated Bloomberg histories, the 2-year yield rose 14.2 basis points to 4.898%, the 5-year 16.7 to 5.004%, the 10-year 15.2 to 5.115%, and the 30-year 10.0 to 5.401%. The 2s30s slope narrowed 4.2 basis points to 50.3 as the shorter sectors absorbed more of the adjustment. The 10-year real yield rose 13.2 basis points to 2.77%, while its breakeven rose 2.0 basis points to 2.345%. Higher real yields accounted for most of the nominal benchmark's daily change in that same-source decomposition, even as the energy shock remained a major policy concern. During the session, Bloomberg described the 10-year trading near 5.13% after a rise of almost 17 basis points and the 30-year around 5.4%; those intraday descriptions need not be treated as exact levels for the dated series.

The move transmitted quickly to financing conditions. The Mortgage Bankers Association said the contract rate on a 30-year fixed mortgage rose 15 basis points to 7.12% in the week ended September 18, its highest since May 2024. Applications fell 1.5% after a 4.1% decline the previous week; the overall application index dropped to 227.3 from 230.8, refinancing to 611.0 from 627.1 and purchase applications to 154.9 from 156.2. The 5-year adjustable mortgage rate moved the other way, falling 13 basis points to 6.1%, so the weekly financing change was not uniform. Redfin's Daryl Fairweather identified the 7% threshold as a psychological deterrent, while Nationwide expected rates around that level through year-end. The new mortgage reading predates Wednesday's Treasury close and shows the housing constraint already in place before the latest yield rise.

The Treasury announced a Thursday purchase of up to $6 billion of securities maturing in 20 to 30 years under Secretary Scott Bessent's expanded buyback program. That is triple the $2 billion size initially communicated in August; the department subsequently said it would at least double such operations. Longer bonds nevertheless sold off after the announcement, with the 30-year yield reaching a reported session high of 5.38% at that point. The earlier expanded operation had purchased about $5.2 billion against a $6 billion maximum after investors offered $10.5 billion; officials cited a lack of competitive bids for leaving capacity unused. The Institute of International Finance argued Wednesday that secondary-market purchases may offer temporary relief but cannot fix the fiscal drivers of rising debt. Thursday's maximum authorizes an operation; it does not establish how much will actually be bought.

Dollar strength was another expression of the U.S. rate repricing. The Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index gained 0.6% in the session account and reached its highest since late July; the 5 p.m. Dollar Index observation rose 0.68% to 101.115. Gold futures fell 1.16% to $4,325.80 and the S&P 500 declined 0.76% to 7,706.03. The Nasdaq 100 was down less than 0.01% in the 5 p.m. market series, while semiconductor shares rose 0.81%, a reminder that the equity response was not uniform even as higher discount rates weighed on broad risk assets. The iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF fell 1.6% to a record closing low of $80.46. Its price has lost more than half its 2020 peak, although its year-to-date total return, which includes distributions, was down 4.8% rather than the 7.7% decline in its share price.

## Global Activity and Policy Diverge Under the Energy Shock

The OECD's new interim outlook broadened the inflation issue beyond the U.S. The organization raised its 2026 global growth forecast to 2.9% from 2.8%, after 3.4% growth in 2025, but lowered 2027 growth to 3.0% from 3.1%. It lifted its G20 inflation forecast to 4.1% for 2026 from 4.0% and to 3.6% for 2027 from 3.1%. Its 2027 inflation revisions covered every G20 economy except China and Saudi Arabia. AI investment supported the near-term activity forecast while persistent energy costs weakened the later outlook.

The OECD projected one more Fed increase this year, further modest rises in the euro area, Australia and South Korea, and additional increases in Japan; it expected the Bank of England and Bank of Canada to hold for now. Its U.S. growth forecasts were 2.2% in 2026 and 2.1% in 2027, with inflation at 3.6% and 2.6%. The organization's downside scenario combined energy stress, a strong El Niño, higher government-bond yields and disappointing AI returns; together they could subtract 0.7 percentage point from 2027 global growth and add 1.1 points to inflation. That was a scenario, not its central forecast. The OECD also warned governments that higher bond yields made repair of public finances more urgent.

Europe's own September business survey showed why the European Central Bank could not treat the energy shock as an automatic reason to stop tightening. The euro-area composite PMI rose to 53.1 from 52.0, against a forecast decline to 51.7, its best level in more than three years. Services improved unexpectedly; Germany's activity grew at its fastest since October 2025, while France expanded at its quickest in more than two years. Manufacturing benefited from AI and defense spending, according to S&P Global's Chris Williamson, and order books across manufacturing and services pointed to continued momentum. Rising costs and borrowing rates still threatened consumption, but the fresh reading gave the ECB a stronger current activity baseline. The euro weakened despite the survey, touching $1.1409 as options positioning increasingly favored downside; market participants attributed the pressure to renewed U.S. rate expectations and Europe's energy exposure.

ECB Chief Economist Philip Lane supplied a qualification to the tightening case. He said the energy surge had not produced significant wage pressure, easing concern that headline inflation was becoming embedded through pay. Yet he described energy prices as tracking the ECB's adverse scenario through mid-2027 before moving toward its baseline, and natural-gas storage at about 70%, 16 percentage points below the historical average. Euro-area inflation was above 3% in August, with some economists seeing 4% by year-end. Lane said the peak rate implied by market prices would be only just above 3% next year after removing risk premia, consistent with roughly two further moves rather than a literal reading of prices as three or four. That distinction tempers the apparent hawkishness of market pricing without dismissing the energy risk.

Britain's outlook joined slower growth to a tighter fiscal constraint. The OECD forecast U.K. expansion of 1.1% in 2026 and 1.0% in 2027, with inflation averaging 3.1% and 2.6%. It judged the BOE able to hold its 3.75% policy rate until mid-2027 before a quarter-point cut, but urged stronger efforts to contain and redirect spending. Economists estimated that higher borrowing costs and inflation had already halved Chancellor John Healey's £23.6 billion buffer against the fiscal rules. Prime Minister Andy Burnham reiterated that the country was overexposed to bond markets and stood by his earlier criticism of being “in hock” to them, while saying he wanted a more productive state. His comments came ahead of the October 28 budget, when planned defense and social spending must meet the deteriorated interest-cost arithmetic. The reported 30-year gilt yield was 5.76%, below a near-6% peak the previous week; the day's global rise in yields did not by itself establish a new U.K.-specific fiscal selloff.

South Africa delivered a completed policy decision. The South African Reserve Bank unanimously raised its benchmark 25 basis points to 7.25%, the second increase this year and the outcome expected by 19 of 22 surveyed economists. Governor Lesetja Kganyago said the bank needed inflation to return to its 3% target as the present shock faded. August inflation had edged to 4.4% from 4.3%; the bank lifted its 2026 average forecast to 4.4% from 4.0% and its 2027 projection to 4.0% from 3.8%. Its assumed oil price rose to $90 a barrel this year from $82 and to $80 next year from $75. Officials had considered holding and a 50-basis-point increase as well as the chosen move. Kganyago described policy as only marginally restrictive before the vote and warned that sustained shocks were more likely to generate second-round effects. The rand weakened about 1.3% to 16.39 per dollar in the reported Johannesburg afternoon, and the 10-year bond yield rose 9 basis points to 8.90%.

Indonesia chose a different defense against the same external pressure. Bank Indonesia held its key rate at 5.75% for a third meeting, as 33 of 36 economists expected, while Governor Destry Damayanti increased incentives to retain capital. The bank cut premiums for conventional hedging swaps by up to 25% and for domestic nondeliverable forwards by up to 30%, with larger discounts for longer-held funds. It also maintained offshore and onshore intervention, including secondary-market purchases of government debt. The rupiah strengthened 0.4% to about 17,800 per dollar and bonds held earlier gains after the decision. Destry said the rate remained adequate for stability, but noted oil above $100 in the trading context, higher global inflation and likely further Fed tightening. August domestic inflation of 3.2% was near the top of the bank's 1.5%-3.5% range, while bank lending grew 13.65% from a year earlier, above its 8%-12% expectation. Lombard Odier's Homin Lee still expected a quarter-point December increase if energy and Fed uncertainty continued.

Singapore's August inflation added another Asian price observation. Core inflation reached 2.2% from a year earlier, its highest since September 2024 and in line with survey expectations, as food, retail and services costs accelerated. Headline inflation was 2.3%, and utilities and other fuels rose 6.1%. The Monetary Authority of Singapore and trade ministry judged risks tilted upward because oil, weather and imported input costs could pass through over coming quarters. The MAS forecast core inflation of 1.5%-2.5% this year and moderation from around mid-2027; its next policy decision is due in mid-October. The current figure therefore speaks to imported inflation pressure without predetermining another exchange-rate-policy adjustment.

Japan remained closed for the Silver Week holiday, leaving its bond-market response to the U.S. selloff for Thursday's reopen. The yen's four-day decline raised intervention concern after the Bank of Japan's recent increase to 1.25%. Eastspring Investments supplied a separate cross-market demand assessment: portfolio manager Rong Ren Goh said a 30-year JGB yielding above 4%, swapped into a developed-market currency including dollars, could offer a currency-hedged yield 100-200 basis points above the comparable base-currency bond. He cited a Japanese 2s30s slope exceeding 200 basis points, against about 80 on average in other core developed markets, as the manager built ultra-long Japanese exposure through high-quality corporate and Samurai debt. That is an attributed strategy and comparison, not an observed Thursday JGB return.

## AI Financing Prices Through a Harder Credit Market

SoftBank's large transaction progressed from preliminary demand to final borrowing terms. The Japanese group raised roughly $11 billion across dollar and euro junk bonds for its AI ambitions, becoming the world's largest corporate junk-bond borrower in Bloomberg's compilation. Its $1 billion 3.5-year dollar tranche yielded 8.625%, a $4.5 billion 5.5-year tranche yielded 9.25%, and another $4.5 billion due in 7.5 years yielded 9.75%. It also sold €1 billion in four- and six-year notes, with the longer euro tranche yielding 8%. The dollar yields were the highest SoftBank had paid in that currency, and the longer euro yield set a tenor record for its euro borrowing.

Orders for the $10 billion dollar portion exceeded $30 billion in Asian afternoon indications, enabling lower yields than initial marketing ranges. The result thus showed access to deep demand, but at a much higher absolute cost than the company previously faced as benchmark Treasury rates rose. SoftBank's commitments to OpenAI approach $65 billion; it had already been extending secured and bridge financing, making the unsecured deal an important test of how much AI exposure bondholders would absorb. Goldman Sachs strategists put global AI-related debt issuance above $575 billion in 2026. SoftBank's 5-year default-swap cost had risen this month to its highest since April 2025, an indication of investor concern alongside the bond orders.

The smaller Digital Drive deal gave a different measure of AI construction risk. A developer sponsored by Blue Owl Capital affiliates, Cedarwood Investment Group and PowerHouse Data Centers raised $1.1 billion in 5-year junk bonds at 98.5 cents on the dollar to yield 9.25%. That was roughly 2.7 percentage points above the average for similarly rated debt. The proceeds support a 76-megawatt campus near Richmond, Virginia, fully leased to CoreWeave under a 15-year, $2.94 billion contract, with operations expected to start in 2027-2028. S&P assigned a BB- rating and identified reliance on one speculative-grade tenant as the principal risk. The long lease supports projected revenue, but construction and tenant credit still determined the financing price.

Hedging activity around established AI borrowers was also changing market structure. Protection traded on $6.9 billion of Nvidia debt in the latest six months, against $640 million in the preceding six, according to S&P Dow Jones Indices' Nicholas Godec citing DTCC data. Nvidia entered the latest CDX investment-grade series on Monday chiefly because of that increase in swap liquidity after its $25 billion June bond sale. SpaceX also joined following a similarly sized high-grade sale. Nvidia protection costs had doubled this year amid its borrowing and infrastructure commitments, while investors and banks used the contracts to hedge accumulated exposure. The CDX roll itself, together with higher Treasury yields, contributed to index widening; a change in its constituent mix cannot be read solely as new deterioration in each borrower's credit.

The broader U.S. credit market softened even while deals cleared. Investment-grade spreads were modestly wider and high-yield spreads noticeably wider at the close. On a distribution-adjusted return basis, LQD fell 1.14% and HYG 0.74%; those fund losses include the effect of higher underlying yields. A prospective Peloton debut showed how borrower-specific terms were being tested: Goldman Sachs had sounded investors on a possible $800 million secured bond yielding about 8%, but no final sale decision had been made. Peloton previously used a $1 billion leveraged loan in 2024 priced about 6 percentage points above its benchmark. The proposed bond's yield was a marketing discussion, not a transaction result.

Other completed or announced sales were more conventional but added useful pricing points. AerCap Funding priced $1.5 billion of senior unsecured debt, split evenly between 5.500% notes due 2030 and 5.875% notes due 2033, fully guaranteed by AerCap Holdings and specified subsidiaries. Proceeds may finance or refinance aircraft assets, repay debt or support general corporate purposes. After the U.S. fixed-income cutoff, Royal Bank of Canada announced a separate $1.5 billion non-viability contingent-capital subordinated issue. Its coupon is 4.67% to October 1, 2031, then compounded CORRA plus 1.16 percentage points to October 1, 2036; a par redemption from 2031 requires supervisory approval and notice. The expected October 1 closing and reset terms define the bank-capital exposure, while the later announcement did not cause Wednesday's Treasury move.

Paramount Skydance's acquisition financing advanced by a narrower step. Citigroup scheduled Thursday loan-investor calls for the $110 billion Warner Bros. Discovery takeover after related lawsuits were settled. The underwritten distribution includes about $30 billion of investment-grade bonds, $7.5 billion of investment-grade loans and roughly $12 billion of second-lien bonds. The structure and the acquisition's interest-rate exposure had already been established; the new calls mark the start of direct investor marketing, with eventual clearing costs still to be set. Separately, messaging firm Bird.com raised $450 million led by JPMorgan, comprising a $400 million term loan and $50 million revolver. Chief Executive Robert Vis said proceeds would fund a dividend to shareholders and current and former employees, giving them liquidity without a secondary share sale. He put last year's EBITDA at $165 million and U.S. revenue at about 70% of the total. The loan therefore funds a payout rather than a new operating asset.

## Restructuring Terms and Sovereign Funding Come Into Focus

Thames Water's senior creditors prepared a larger concession package to avoid government special administration. London & Valley Water, including Elliott, Silver Point and Farallon, plans a revised proposal as soon as October after discussions with regulator Ofwat and officials. The debt write-down under discussion rises to about 35% from 30%, while proposed new equity increases from £3.35 billion to about £3.5 billion. Roughly £6.55 billion of debt would accompany that equity. The figures remain subject to negotiation, but the change in creditor loss sharing is the current development in a utility with more than £18 billion of debt.

The group also proposes more than £1 billion for a dedicated performance fund, at least £200 million above the sum previously offered in place of some regulatory penalties. Thames is expected to incur up to £800 million of performance penalties by decade-end for leaks, sewage spills and other missed targets; those sums would normally reduce customers' bills. Creditors argue that ring-fencing more money to fix operations would give the utility a better route back to investment grade than taking the cash out through penalties. Legal fines for environmental or drinking-water breaches remain separate and payable. The package would also grant the government a golden share, strengthen oversight and bar owner dividends during a proposed nine-year turnaround. Lawmakers have objected to handing control to creditors, and the government is considering special administration. A prior Teneo analysis estimated Class A creditor recoveries as low as about 50 pence per pound in that scenario, depending on operating performance; that is a scenario estimate, not an agreed restructuring recovery.

Swiss lawmakers made an actual capital decision with a different effect on bank creditors. The upper house voted 29-16 for a rule requiring UBS to back foreign subsidiaries with high-quality equity equal to as much as 90% of their value, just below the government's original 100% proposal. UBS estimated about $16 billion of additional CET1 at its domestic unit; Goldman Sachs and Citi analysts put the burden around $17 billion. UBS had urged a less onerous alternative using much more additional contingent-convertible AT1 debt. That avenue narrowed after the vote, and existing UBS AT1 bonds rose as much as 0.3 cent to 98.36 cents as the prospect of extra issuance receded. UBS said it would continue opposing the bill. The lower house must still take a position, and a final rule may not arrive before 2027 or could go to a referendum.

Venezuela's debt discussions gained direct U.S. presidential involvement. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said President Trump and interim President Delcy Rodríguez discussed restructuring at a September 22 reception, alongside the institutional steps needed for future elections. Rubio said the United States wanted to help stabilize the economy, but debt treatment had to be done properly. Venezuelan sovereign and PDVSA defaulted bonds total about $60 billion; analysts' broader estimate of $150 billion-$200 billion includes accrued interest and other liabilities, including arbitration claims. The distinction between bond principal and total claims matters for potential creditor recoveries. The countries had already begun multilateral engagement, and the Inter-American Development Bank's proposed $2.5 billion loan still faced resistance from some directors. No restructuring terms or financing approval emerged from the meeting.

Hungarian government debt offered a contrasting case of foreign demand. The central bank's decision to lower its long-run inflation target to 2.5% from 3% effective in 2028 was already known; the new contribution was the reported scale of inflows and their effect on yields. Deutsche Bank estimated $13.5 billion of foreign purchases of local bonds year to date, including $10 billion after the April election. Debt agency AKK put foreign holdings at 34% at August's end, the highest since 2019. Hungary's 10-year yield was about 5.64%, below Poland's 6.16% and Romania's 7.29%, as investors linked the new target to possible euro convergence. That demand depends on fiscal execution: the 2026 deficit is projected at 7.5% of GDP, and investors are awaiting the 2027 budget and medium-term plan. Potential release of about €16 billion of EU funds is another support, not a completed payment.

China supplied a more immediate money-market measure. The People's Bank of China announced that overnight reverse repos of up to 1 trillion yuan, about $149 billion, per day would be available from September 28 through October 8 around the Mid-Autumn and National Day holidays. It did not specify individual operation days or the borrowing cost. The interbank bond market is due to close September 25-27 and October 1-7, making the facility a backstop for cash and settlement needs across an extended holiday period. Bank Indonesia's simultaneous reliance on hedging incentives and bond purchases illustrated another local response to external-rate pressure, but the Chinese operation addresses calendar liquidity rather than a policy-rate change.

U.S.-China trade risk shifted after the bond-market cutoff. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Washington and Beijing had agreed September 23 to extend their Busan agreement through January 10 following his discussion with Vice Premier He Lifeng ahead of Xi Jinping's Washington visit. Bessent said the parties considered whether a larger agreement could replace a string of narrower deals. The extension reduced the immediate risk of the framework expiring; the announcement came too late to explain the completed U.S. fixed-income move, and the broader agreement remained an objective rather than a concluded transaction.

## Forward Market Significance

Thursday's Treasury operation will show how much of the announced $6 billion maximum for 20- to 30-year bonds the department actually buys and at what prices investors offer securities. The next 7-year auction provides a separate test of coupon demand after the 5-year sale's 3.1-basis-point tail. Those outcomes can distinguish Wednesday's auction-specific weakness from a more sustained increase in the concession required for new duration.

U.S. initial and continuing jobless claims on September 24 will test Barr's judgment that labor-market risks have receded. The supplied expectations are 201,000 initial claims after 196,000 and 1.750 million continuing claims after 1.730 million. Friday's durable-goods report has a 0.4% headline decline expected, against gains of 0.6% excluding transport and 0.5% in nondefense capital goods excluding aircraft; that split will matter after the PMI's broad order increase. The final September Michigan survey carries expected one-year inflation expectations of 4.6% and five-year expectations of 3.4%, a direct test of whether rising input costs are reaching households' longer horizon. Fed Presidents John Williams and Tom Barkin are scheduled to speak Thursday, with Barkin's next qualification particularly relevant after his earlier conditional account of repeated supply shocks.

The U.S.-Iran talks still face the stated dispute over sanctions, the U.S. blockade and freedom of navigation through Hormuz. Actual passage and sustained export flows would matter more for the inflation outlook than another meeting announcement. The Trump-Xi summit follows the newly extended trade framework; investors will be able to judge whether the leaders agree to broader tariff, investment or technology terms before January 10. Neither prospective development is part of Wednesday's completed bond close.

Elsewhere, Japan's return from holiday will reveal how JGBs and the yen absorb both the BOJ's higher policy-rate floor and Wednesday's U.S. duration selloff. Norges Bank's closely divided decision and the Riksbank's expected hold, both due Thursday with updated forecasts, will test whether higher energy costs are producing divergent Scandinavian rate paths. Thames Water's revised creditor proposal, Hungary's 2027 budget plan and the actual marketing terms of Paramount's multi-part debt package remain separate credit and sovereign tests whose numbers, approvals and timing will determine the next change in bondholder exposure.

Barr said inflation risk had increased and further Fed tightening was likely needed; October hike odds rose after his remarks. A $70 billion 5-year auction cleared 3.1 basis points above its when-issued yield, amplifying the Treasury selloff. The 10-year yield rose 15.2 basis points to 5.115%, largely through a rise in real yields. A 7.12% weekly mortgage rate showed a housing constraint already in place before Wednesday’s close.

section_summaries.section_title: Global Activity and Policy Diverge Under the Energy Shock
section_summaries.summary: The OECD raised its 2026 global growth forecast to 2.9% but cut 2027 to 3.0% and lifted inflation projections as persistent energy costs threaten later activity. A stronger euro-area PMI gave the ECB a firmer activity baseline, while Philip Lane said energy had yet to cause significant wage pressure. South Africa raised its rate to 7.25%; Indonesia held at 5.75% and eased hedging costs to retain capital. Britain faces a narrower fiscal buffer ahead of its October 28 budget.

section_summaries.section_title: AI Financing Prices Through a Harder Credit Market
section_summaries.summary: SoftBank raised roughly $11 billion in dollar and euro junk bonds for its AI ambitions. Strong orders let it lower yields from initial guidance, yet its dollar tranches still carried the highest borrowing yields it has paid in that currency. Digital Drive’s $1.1 billion data-center bond yielded 9.25% amid construction and single-tenant risk. U.S. investment-grade spreads widened modestly and high-yield spreads widened noticeably, while Nvidia protection trading rose alongside its borrowing and infrastructure commitments.

section_summaries.section_title: Restructuring Terms and Sovereign Funding Come Into Focus
section_summaries.summary: Thames Water creditors are preparing a revised proposal with about a 35% debt write-down and £3.5 billion of new equity, still subject to negotiation. Swiss lawmakers advanced a rule requiring UBS to back foreign subsidiaries with equity equal to as much as 90% of their value. Venezuela’s debt entered direct presidential talks without agreed restructuring terms; foreign inflows supported Hungarian bonds, while China announced a holiday liquidity backstop.

Thursday’s long-bond buyback and the next 7-year auction will test Treasury demand after the weak 5-year sale. U.S. claims, durable goods and Michigan inflation expectations will probe the growth and inflation picture behind Barr’s tightening case. Actual passage through Hormuz and sustained export flows matter more for energy-driven inflation than another talks announcement; Japan’s reopen and Thames Water’s revised terms offer separate bond-market tests.

overall_summary.headline: Treasuries sell off as strong U.S. activity, Fed tightening signals and weak auction demand converge
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries sold off across the coupon curve on September 23. The 10-year yield rose 15.2 basis points to 5.115% and the 5-year climbed 16.7 basis points to 5.004%. September’s flash U.S. composite PMI reached 58.4, with faster new orders and a sharp increase in input costs. Fed Governor Michael Barr said inflation risks had risen as labor-market risks receded and further tightening was likely needed. The $70 billion 5-year auction then cleared at 5.033%, 3.1 basis points above its when-issued yield, adding a concrete sign of weak demand to a selloff already under way. Higher real yields accounted for most of the 10-year benchmark’s daily rise.

Oil recovered above $100 during trading as Iran reiterated conditions on passage through Hormuz, although Brent was down 1.40% at the 5 p.m. New York observation. The dollar strengthened, the S&P 500 fell 0.76%, and U.S. investment-grade spreads widened modestly while high-yield spreads widened noticeably. SoftBank still completed roughly $11 billion of dollar and euro junk-bond financing for its AI ambitions, but at its highest dollar borrowing yields. The next 7-year auction and Thursday’s Treasury buyback will show whether the supply strain persists.
